title: Let Codex fix a bug while you watch
goal: You will reproduce a project bug, have Codex investigate and fix it, review and test the diff, and commit the verified change.
prerequisites: A Git project with a reproducible bug
Codex CLI installed and signed in
The project's test or run command

steps.action: Run the smallest command that reproduces the bug.
steps.where: Terminal prompt at the root of the Git project.
steps.why: A concrete failure gives Codex evidence to investigate and a result to verify later.
steps.checkpoint: The terminal shows the incorrect behavior or failing test you intend to fix.
hint_levels: Start with the command closest to the symptom.
Use a focused test, build, or run command instead of the entire suite when possible.
At the project-root prompt, enter the relevant command, such as npm test -- path/to/failing.test.js.

steps.action: Launch Codex in the project directory.
steps.where: Terminal prompt at the root of the Git project.
steps.why: Starting here gives Codex access to the repository and its local instructions.
steps.checkpoint: The Codex interactive prompt appears and identifies the current project directory.
hint_levels: Stay in the directory containing the repository.
The CLI starts from your current terminal location.
At the project-root prompt, type codex and press Enter.

steps.action: Describe the symptom and ask Codex to investigate before editing.
steps.where: Codex interactive prompt at the bottom of the terminal.
steps.why: Supplying the exact failure while separating investigation from implementation makes the diagnosis easier to review.
steps.checkpoint: Codex begins inspecting relevant files or running diagnostic commands without immediately changing code.
hint_levels: Include what you expected and what actually happened.
Give Codex the reproduction command and ask for a root-cause explanation before any edit.
Enter: Investigate this bug without editing yet: [symptom]. Expected: [result]. Actual: [result]. Reproduce with: [command]. Explain the root cause.

steps.action: Approve the safe read-only commands Codex proposes while following its investigation.
steps.where: Approval prompt inside the Codex terminal session.
steps.why: The command output shows whether the investigation follows evidence from the real project.
steps.checkpoint: You can see Codex connect command results and source locations to a specific root cause.
hint_levels: Check what each proposed command will inspect.
Allow searches, file reads, and the reproduction command when their scope matches the project.
At each approval prompt, review the displayed command and choose the option that approves this command only.

steps.action: Tell Codex to implement the smallest fix for the diagnosed cause.
steps.where: Codex interactive prompt beneath the investigation summary.
steps.why: A narrowly scoped instruction reduces unrelated changes and makes review safer.
steps.checkpoint: Codex reports edited file names and the terminal shows that changes were applied.
hint_levels: Refer back to the diagnosis you just reviewed.
Ask for the minimal change and explicitly rule out unrelated refactoring.
Enter: Implement the smallest fix for that root cause; preserve existing behavior and avoid unrelated refactors.

steps.action: Ask Codex to display and explain the complete diff without making further edits.
steps.where: Codex interactive prompt in the terminal.
steps.why: Reviewing every changed line catches accidental scope expansion before you keep the fix.
steps.checkpoint: A diff with added and removed lines is visible, along with an explanation of how it addresses the bug.
hint_levels: Pause implementation and inspect what changed.
Request the full Git diff plus a file-by-file explanation.
Enter: Do not edit anything else; show the complete git diff and explain how each change fixes the symptom.

steps.action: Run the original reproduction command again from the Codex session.
steps.where: Codex interactive prompt and its command-output area.
steps.why: Repeating the same check demonstrates that the observed bug is actually resolved.
steps.checkpoint: The formerly failing test passes or the incorrect behavior no longer appears in the command output.
hint_levels: Use the exact check that failed at the beginning.
Tell Codex to run the original command and report its exit status.
Enter: Run [original command] again and show the result and exit status.

steps.action: Exit Codex and commit only the reviewed fix.
steps.where: Codex prompt, followed by the project-root terminal prompt.
steps.why: A Git commit preserves the verified fix as an intentional project change.
steps.checkpoint: The terminal shows a successful commit summary, and git status reports a clean working tree.
hint_levels: Return to the shell, stage the reviewed files, and record them.
Use /exit, then git add with explicit file paths, git commit, and git status.
Enter /exit, then run git add path/to/reviewed-file, git commit -m "Fix <bug symptom>", and git status.
